text: This is a worse version of Panera. Panera sucks. Honestly, that's probably all you really need to know right there, but I will of course elaborate... We had seen this place pop up and were somewhat excited to give them a try. Wound up in the area randomly and were hungry for breakfast, but wanted it on the go. Kneaders has a drive-thru so we figured it was worth a try. I went with the reuben panini, and my wife got the harvest vegetable sandwich. We both got chocolate croissants and I got a large iced tea, she had a coffee with cream. The best items were the croissants. Not the best I've ever had but they were nice. They were light and crispy on the outside, the chocolate had a nice flavor. In descending order, I think my wife's sandwich was the second best item, but it was a little odd. The roasted vegetables were good, and the bread was good, but there was a cheese on it that you would think and expect to be cream cheese that turns out to be ricotta. And its not like super high-grade ricotta either. It made the sandwich weird. From there, the food is a drastic drop off in flavor and quality. My reuben was thin, soggy, and one of the worst sandwiches I've had in a long time. I thought this was supposed to be a panini...You know, like crispy on the outside? No. It was complete mushy awfulness. Both of our sandwiches came with potato chips that were not cooked all the way through, so they were crispy on the outside and soft once you bit into them. Terrible. My wife's coffee was clearly burnt and my iced tea had no ice. The only vaguely redeeming factor to this place was that the people working there were very nice. And the croissants were good. Apart from that, everything was just awful. This is not a chain that is going to survive in Tucson, I'd like to think we have higher standards.

text: Copeland's has been a favorite of mine for years and I would visit the one in Kenner every time I'm in town. I grew up in Kenner/Metairie and visit 2-3 times per year. I looked forward to my Copeland's meal more than any others. Sadly, the Kenner location has been going downhill. The past few times I've been there, the service, and even worse, the way the manager ignores issues, has not been good. To make a long story short, there were 5 negatives during one last visit that finally convinced me not to go back, all of which would have been forgiven and forgotten if the manager would have had any semblance of caring, and would not have been so rude and dismissive. I'll spare you the verbose details, but here's the gist of it... -- First, this might sound trivial to some, but the plastic menus were so sticky they stuck to our fingers (so much that mine made noise every time I peeled my fingers off of it) -- not very appetizing as you peruse the delicious food offerings. -- A very simple request of "no onions" on a hickory sauce burger turned into a situation where the burger was eventually eaten ice cold, with a cold side of hickory sauce, after everyone else had finished their meals. With no apologies from anyone at any point. (The onions had mixed in with the sauce and cheese, so we couldn't brush them off easily.) -- The original food order took 45 minutes to arrive (and was barely warm), the failed attempt at correcting the burger issue took three steps and another 15-20 minutes. -- A to-go order placed plenty early was forgotten and didn't arrive until 20 minutes after we paid the bill. -- The chef was wandering around the restaurant and then sitting comfortably in the bar involved in a lengthy conversation with the bartender, while customers were waiting to order drinks and food orders were being botched. -- The manager eventually stopped by the table (of his own accord) and asked if there was a problem, but when we chose to nicely share the situation, he offered an insincere apology and walked away uninterested, not even offering to remind the staff to be more attentive or offering a complimentary dessert or drink (not that we wanted it, but a gesture goes a long way). Keep in mind that I've loved Copeland's for years. I'm sad that this location has been slipping, and now it's off my list. I hope the problems are addressed, because I will miss it. Clean your sticky menus off, for a start.
label: NEG

text: Made an advance reservation one week out for my wife's 50th birthday celebration weekend. At the time of reservation I was showed a table, that the hostess recommended for our special night. Upon arriving for the scheduled reservation, we were told that the section previously agreed upon was closed. We were seated on the main dining floor at a densely placed four top, right on top of another four top. Service started out great: knowledgeable descriptions of drinks, menu, etc. We began with cocktails and proceeded to order our entrees. After that, the service deteriorated. Let me back up. Ocean Prime uses a quasi team approach: server, expediter and bus/water person. Our salads arrived with only two of three guest receiving their salads. One person ordered salad only, so fair enough... I understand the timing. The entrees and "sides" were brought to our table by the expediter with no serving spoons for the sides or "duh" steaks knives for the filets. By this time, our server was busy attending to a large section of the main dining floor and had just been seated a booth with six people. Needless to say, we were not on his radar. There was an individual running drinks from the bar, but NO ONE ever checked back once our food was ordered. Really? This is serving 101 and for crying out loud, Applebee's knows that. Finally, the server's attention is grabbed, (should one really have to flag) as he passed by our table. My wife (Birthday Girl) is using her fork to serve the mashed potatoes side from a bowl. I mention to the server, as he is holding a tray with side dishes and serving spoons (for the booth of six next to us) that we did not receive serving spoons. He looks at the mashed potatoes and corn side and says, "Would you like a spoon?" Double duh! That was the first check back we had, customer initiated, well into our meal. Oh, our glasses of water are empty and the salad plates are clearly finished and remain unnoticed, sitting on the table. As the server made his way through the dining room, we flagged him a second time for water, literally begging for service. Here is the kicker, the server finally acknowledged the birthday occasion (The very reason we selected Ocean Prime) and said he would like to buy my wife a desert. My rub with this approach: 1 - Horrible service the entire night. 2 - Servers that have ignored you all night, then endear themselves at the end for gratuity sake. 3 - We literally waited 15 minutes for the "complimentary"creme brûlée once ordered Needless to say we had an awful experience on a very special and monumental birthday. Just to lend contrast,the preceding evening we went to Vetri. It was going to be a weekend celebration with Saturday at Vetri and Sunday at Ocean Prime. I just have to say, there could not have been a more stark contrast as to what "Great" looks like. On the way out of the restaurant I inquired as to when the GM would be back in? Suspecting something was wrong, the assistant manager (Where was she on the dining floor all night?) ask about our dining experience. I proceeded to let her know how our evening went or rather... did not. She offered free desert and the obligatory, "Come back and join us again and give us another chance" excuses and cop-outs. She lamented that Ocean Prime wants to deliver a 5 star experience and it is clear you did not get a 5 star experience. Triple duh...Really?? Big customer service tip: Make it right in the moment, because someone who has had such a poor experience does not want a free desert nor are they likely to take you up on your offer to return. My wife, who is the epitome of patience, even mentioned in her kind words, "How off the service was". Could not have been more disappointed in Ocean Prime. #oceanprime

text: My Mother had prearranged her cremation with Curlew. She was 87 and while she was certainly at an age where her death was not a total surprise, it was still unexpected. When she died suddenly I came to Florida to wrap up her affairs and my first order of business was to meet with a Curlew representative. Considering the circumstances we had a pleasant conversation. I related a couple stories about my mother who had a very good sense of humor. The last story I will be able to tell about her was that in the last 3 or 4 months before her death she had been in the process of getting new dentures. When she told me it was going to cost $10,000.00 I thought that was rather expensive. I wondered if, at 87, she would get her return on investment. But it was her money. She got them a week and a half before she died. Her friends have told me they looked fabulous. In retrospect I really should have had an open casket with a big smile on her face. Since I had never been in a situation like this before I had some questions about cremation. I commented I had heard they removed pace makers prior to cremation and was curious as to why; perhaps they exploded? I was told they sell them to South America. Old buses, trolley cars and planes I knew about but pace makers were a surprise. We chatted a while longer and she asked if I'd like my Mother's $10,000.00 teeth. I thought about it for a couple minutes and thought what the hell, those suckers would have put a new roof on my house. So I said yes, I'll take them home with me and put them on display in my curio cabinet, They'll be the most expensive collectible I have and I'm sure my Mother would have had a chuckle about it. I was told it would be take care of. So then I was given some forms to sign, typical stuff, signatures here, initial these items, yada yada yada. So I did, without reading as I'm sure most people do in those circumstances. I was told I could pick up her cremains in a few days. When I went to pick up I didn't think about the teeth. When I got home I looked in the tasteful blue tote bag the box of ashes were in but didn't see the teeth. When I contacted the representative a day or two later to request a couple documents I asked about them. Her response only addressed my request for the documents. At this point I had my hands full with a lot of other stuff and the teeth and documents were not a priority. I figured I'd get them at a later date. When I emailed my contact in March I received an email from Steve Harris the funeral home director advising that the representative I had been dealing with was no longer employed by Curlew and that my request for the teeth had not been received until after the cremation. I responded that there was apparently a problem as I had been told it would be taken care of well before the cremation. Mr. Harris' immediate response was to send me a copy of the documents I had signed and initialed. He commented that "if" there had been such a conversation regarding the teeth it was never documented and then he stated I had signed "I/We understand that if I wish to remove and/or retain any items from the remains, I must do so directly or by authorized person prior to the cremation process". "You initialed that line and signed this document." He concluded "It is an unfortunate circumstance that this incident has occurred. I hope that this will help to clarify our position." At best I can only regard this as a rather cavalier response to the situation. I replied that he had made his position crystal clear and it was most distressing. To say the least it is an unfortunate circumstance. And fortunately, or apparently unfortunately, I was in a situation I had never experienced before. I was totally relying on the integrity of Curlew's staff for guidance. Trusting that I signed and initialed where instructed, obviously without thorough review. I am sure that is probably the circumstance with 99.9% of their customers. The potential for problems never crossed my mind. Had I known that the veracity of my conversation with their representative might even be questioned or require documentation I would have arranged for a videographer to record our meeting. When I was told it would be taken care of I assumed that it would be taken care of. I can only surmise that similar problems may well have led to this employee's departure from employment at Curlew. I can only suggest that if you have dealings with Curlew be very, very careful about reading thoroughly and understanding everything you sign. This certainly applies after the fact and probably more importantly when you make any arrangements with them especially if you are in a vulnerable state of mind.
label: NEG

While I was there I only had a limited number of dishes (3) and they were all deserving of plate licking. However, I did resist because it was not that kind of place... The venue itself is quaint, intimate and limited on busy detail, but small. All of which contributes immensely to my dinning experience. We also ordered a bottle of wine which was recommended to us by our lovely food guide, Katie. She brought out two wines for us to try in case we didn't like what we picked, which we didn't, and ordered what she suggested. However, if you like picking out your own wine, you might have difficulty on the limited wine menu. Brick & Mortar is an innovator in St. Pete and I hope other restaurants follow in its wake.

text: Can we get a 6th star for Ezras? Any eatery that makes food so delicious that I would consider changing my diet for is so deserving of a 6th star. I have been trying to rock the Paleo diet for over a year now however, with so many wonderful new dining options in Indy...and my love for beer... it's hard to stay true. Ezra's makes it easy..ier. It's one of a handful of places in Indy I personally feel I can go too, order from the menu, and not have to modify a meal. In addition, who knew Raw Vegan cuisine could be so delicious? I didn't. Every time I visit I tell myself if I could eat like this everyday I would go vegan. It is that good! Good news! They offer classes to learn more. Let's talk food shall we, this is what I have tried so far..... *Buddha Bowl (extremely filling, beets, honey spiced kale, fermented veggies, sunflower sprouts, avocado, tasty raw falafel balls, lemon Tahini dressing). So many wonderful flavors mixing together for an incredible mind blowing salad experience. *Nacho Mamma Bowl (warm beans & quinoa, greens, avocado, and that nacho cheeze! How do you make that cheeze? I want to know! Great dish and very filling. *RaWco Taco Salad (walnut taco meat & that nacho cheeze (again). Served with flax chips that work perfectly to scoop up that nacho cheeze. Best taco salad I have ever had hands down. This one is full of healthy goodness, you just feel good eating it. *Anti-inflammatory Turmeric Quinoa Salad (delicious and so good for you!) Perfect Grab N Go option to eat in between a meeting or a nice side dish. *Herbed Cashew Cheeze (tastes just like cheese but better). Great with flax crackers. I am thinking about adding it to future charcuterie boards for gatherings. Mondays they prep for the week so they only offer Grab N Go. Come early because items sell out quickly. Personal notes: I must try 1 of each of those amazing desserts in the case, the granola bowl, a hot tonic latte, and nourishing shots. Oh my! I have a lot of eating to do!

text: I placed my first order with SPUD after receiving a promo code from one of their friendly representatives at a local food event. With a little bit of credit, I was free to try out SPUD's produce delivery with no hesitation and I'm pleased to say that I'm quite impressed with my experience. My order consisted of mostly fruits and veggies but SPUD also offers baked goods, dairy, meat, juices and various other snacks. I was really impressed by their website's interface which made it easy to choose and review an order. Obviously it's challenging picking out produce online since you can't see the size, shape and colour of your choices but I was happy to try a little bit of everything as part of my first order. The quality of the produce was generally quite good and the order was delivered in a hefty box right to my door. Most of the produce was fresh, large and tasty, however a couple items were a little bit over-ripe. Given how important seeing and touching produce is when you buy it at the store or the market, I was generally quite impressed with what I had delivered and I would definitely use SPUD's services again, especially for heartier items like potatoes, onions, squash and packaged goods. SPUD is a really great resource for people who want to have fresh, organic food delivered but can't make it to the grocery store or won't be able to make it to one of Edmonton's markets on the weekends. It can be tough not being able to see and feel your produce before ordering it online but my first experience has assured me that they pick out great food to deliver to your door.

text: A third-wave coffee shop dedicated to craft, but the ego outweighs the appeal. If you want pretension and arrogance with your coffee, this is your place. Bean selection centers on African coffees, so if that's your favorite than you'll have options. But most other continents are pretty under-represented. The atmosphere is pretty sparse and uncomfortable. I hope you like skulls with beards. There is usually more than one espresso option, which is nice. Milk-based drinks are just average. The pour over coffee is good, but not really any better than a few other places in town--so I choose to pass on the attitude. Went a few times but this was my last experience where I decided I was done (I worked in coffee for 3+ years and have been to great shops in Seattle, Portland, Italy, etc): My wife orders a pour-over and I order a cappuccino, asking the guy taking my order (the owner) to make it just a tiny bit on the dry side. He says doesn't say anything and we go to sit and wait for our drinks. A good while later our drinks arrive, and what do I get? Basically a wet latte. I never do this, but a place that is supposed to be about excellence tips the scale, and I take my drink up to the counter. I tell another barista my problem, very politely (I basically never take back orders), and he says, "Um, yeah, we just don't really make our cappuccinos like that. We go for the silky, 'traditional' approach." Ok sure, I say, "Well that's fine, but that's not what the guy said when I ordered it." He agrees to remake it and I go sit down. The owner comes over, "So, man, I heard you had a problem with your cappuccino." Me, "Well it was just really wet and I asked for it a little dry." He says, "The thing is, ordering a dry cappuccino is like ordering a steak well done." (Never mind that if you order a steak well done, even the best restaurants will bring you a well-done steak, because, you know, that's what you ordered). So I say, "Look, I've worked in coffee. I'm not ordering a light and fluffy starbucks capp with airy foam that weighs 2 ounces. I just asked for it a little on the dry side. If you don't make it that way then tell me so when I order and I'll get something else. I just didn't want a 5 ounce wet latte." He tells me I can have a pour-over and walks away. And that was and will be the last time I visit.
label: NEG

text: BLUF: Very unique place in NOLA. Amazing food. Very nice atmosphere. Great place to go and share food. I like middle-eastern food a lot but always stick to the gyro. this place is very different. it focus on pita and hummus/dippings. They have a lot of options. We got 3 dipping things (not sure what you call them); babaganush, itka, and something else. Not sure how to spell them but they were unbelivably awesome. They come with pita that is made right before they bring it to you. The pita is good enough to eat by itself. We also got 1 hummus; the roasted scallop with pistachio. this was my favorite part of the meal. Pretty big serving; about twice as big as the small dippers listed above with 2 scallops that were fantastic. At the end of the meal they brought out the matza ball soup. They were nice and split the order up for us since there were 2 of us. It would have def been a decent size bowl for one person so i suggest sharing. It was good but matza ball soup can only be but so good in my opinion. It had duck in it which was an awesome touch. Prices are not bad. It was kind of a lite meal since it was soup and pita with dips. We got full but not overly full. They do have big entrees so I would be interested in trying those. However, the dips/hummus was so good I would probably just get those again. The service was good. The atmosphere is very fancy and nice. Awesome bathrooms. Overall the place is so unique to New Orleans that it will always stand out as a good different place to go when feel like something different. Sharing can be fun too (sometimes).

text: I attended a Meetup event at this restaurant last night, and the company and conversation were great! The food and service...not so much. I understand that having a group of 20+ can put some stress on a small restaurant like this, which is the reason I am giving them two stars. The "benefit of the doubt," if you will. My meal started with a soup that was on the specials menu. It was very tasty, but it took it over an hour to make its way to me from the kitchen! Don't restaurants have soups made already, and just ladle them into bowls? Anyway, the delay was surprising and disappointing. For an entree, I chose the vegetable curry. Unfortunately, there were a few notable issues with the entree. First, I was asked if I wanted rice with it. Of course - isn't that what curry is typically served with? They had several varieties of rice, which is nice, but they charge for all of them separately - and they aren't inexpensive. I was a bit shocked that rice wasn't included with the meal. I've never seen that before, in an Indian restaurant. Second, I ordered my curry hot, in terms of spice level. It was the mildest Indian entree I've ever tried - no spice at all. (And when she delivered it, she said "vegetable curry, hot," so I don't think it was a mistake?!?!) Finally, there were very few veggies in the VEGETABLE curry. It contained a couple of carrot slices, and a few green peas. Otherwise, it was all huge chunks of white potato. If I had to use one word to sum it up: bland. I didn't complain about it because I'm not that type of guy, but I don't like being tricked. Strike 2. The reuben sandwich tastes BAD, and there is more saur kraut on it than meat. They also use a Red Rouquefort Dressing, which I really couldn't stand. It just doesn't taste good. They also have trouble with spelling. On their website they call it a "rueben" but it's actually supposed to be "reuben." As for the Gruyere cheese, between their lunch and dinner menus they spell it right once, but also spell it as "Gruyree" and "Greyer." So they have a lack of detail clearly. I know, I know, words are hard. Strike 3. The next day I checked my card transactions and found a charge of $14.34 from this place. Now how can that be? Okay, so it was supposed to be $10 and they charged me $11, I know, and then tax which brought the total to about $12. This means they had to have added a tip. I intentionally did not tip them, so this would be theft. NOT okay. Strike.... 4??? Yes, strike 4 damnit. Screw this place, never coming back. Before they tricked me into paying more for my lunch than their website said I'd have to pay, and before they stole from me, I was going to give them 2 stars based primarily on the bad tasting food, but was going to give them another try. text: I have been a frequent BUYER at this shop for many years. The owner recently expanded into several buildings keeping her furniture in one area and clothing in another. The people who work the counters are very helpful. However, I recently had a very upsetting experience at the shop. It seems as long as you are spending, Diane likes you, but if there is a problem, she treats you horribly. There was a big problem over a $125 item I purchased that had a made up retail tag of $225 on it. Upon arriving home, I looked online for the exact same item # that was on the tag, I found the same items selling for $15 RETAIL. I called immediately after I learned this as I thought that some items were consigned and I wanted to warn the owner that she might have a problem with this consignor/seller. She told me "no returns" and she had purchased this from a shop in Wayne, my home town. I figured this was her way of telling me that I had to take this up with the original seller myself. No, that was not what she wanted. She told me how honest and nice the owner was. She repeated how the person she bought the item from was a very kind person and she knew them well. Then, she told me to come back to the store with tags in tact (they were exactly as given to me) and she would give me a credit ONLY. I understood and it didn't seem like a big problem as I spend quite a bit of money there and have even taken and sent several friends there. I also thought she should look and she would see that the quality was just not there and it had to be a fake. Not once, did I accuse or suggest she sold fake designer items and I wouldn't. I realize she could have made a mistake. We all do. She did want to see the paperwork I found online. I had already saved it for her. Well, I am also a kind hearted, honorable, caring, sincere, generous, and gracious person. However, I was not treated this way. I am open-minded and am hoping this was just a bad day for the owner, but I'm not sure. Upon arriving at the store, I saw her outside and she came up to me to tell me that inside the store, she would give me a store credit. Not once did she apologize or thank me. I was treated as someone less than honest. She was very abrupt, not talking at all (I suppose she did not want customers to know what was happening and I understand that as well), handed me he paper, told me not to lose it because she didn't keep records, and there were no smiles or "please come back." I said I had picked out several items in the furniture part of HER shop so the credit would be spent fast. Then, she said that I could only use the credit in the clothing area, not the furniture area. She is the owner of all of the items in these shops. She does not consign apparently. Instead, she outright buys things so she owns all of the furniture and clothing. I felt as though this was retaliation towards me and a need to be in control, making up this policy to disrespect me. I was humiliated and very sad after being treated this way. I didn't deserve it. I understand policies, but the world is not black and white. It is shades of gray. This was the next day and I thought I was helping her by making her aware. In the past, I have even told her of stores that were going out of business so she could go in and buy there items - giving her a lead to make more money in her business. I guess this goes to show that when you are giving to people they will give you a fake smile. Here, I thought I was valued as a customer. I will go back to the shop and spend my $125 on clothing, even though I had just spent another $60 in the furniture/home goods area, but I guess that doesn't matter. I wonder if when I go back, my credit will only be good on a purse, rather than clothing. Some things don't feel or seem right in how we treat each other. I feel so disappointed, VERY undervalued, and treated in a very condescending, harsh way. At no time was I disingenuous or ungracious. Very sad feeling leaving the shop I used to like so much.

text: If i could have given a 3.5 rating I would - but I felt like rounding up to a 4 was a more accurate reflection of the experiences I've had at Wine Exchange. The Service: More often than not, I am pleased with the service at Wine Exchange (wait time is usually low, food arrives promptly, rarely a rude server), but I have felt like the server just did not want to be a server on several evenings. I am lactose intolerant and also try to gravitate towards gluten-free meals (I know these restrictions are a pain in the neck and I really feel terrible every time I have to inquire about the menu items being gluten free), and the server was obviously not in the mood to cater to my needs. He basically told me he couldn't give me any information on the gluten status of any of the items on the menu (note - I'd had this server at wine exchange several times over the last 5 years, and I know I wasn't the first to ask about gluten). I felt kinda dumb and embarrassed so I ended up ordering a salad that night. Bummer. The Food: hasn't disappointed me yet. I've tried many menu items over the years. One appetizer dish we always go back to is the Baked Brie served with fruit and crostini. Generous portions and great for 4 people to share. I also LOVE the Cuban salad - think a deconstructed Cuban sandwich over iceberg lettuce. Swiss, ham, tomato, and some green olives for good measure. The grilled veggie salad is also on point - I give both salads a 4.5 star rating. As far as pizza goes, I've only tasted the Athenian, and it was good (not great). Wine Exchange typically has a decent specials menu, and I tend to order whatever seafood dish is featured that day. Portions are generous, and fish is always fresh. My husband has also enjoyed the Penne For Your Thoughts (penne with shrimp scallops asparagus etc in a rich lemon butter sauce) a few times. The bread they serve is probably my fav. Restaurant bread in the area. If they don't bring it, make sure you ask for it!

text: I was disappointed after reading all of the great reviews. My "traditional" Cuban sandwich was not what I had hoped for. I should have specified no mayo... only mustard, and maybe some mojo from the pork. I could live without the Salami too.. as that is a something you really only find in Tampa. I have no idea why they call this a "Traditional" Cuban Sandwich. The Deviled crab was huge, and delicious... although a bit gooey inside. The inside was only warm, not hot... although the outside was deep fried to a nice brown crispness. It did have a lot of crab though. Service was good, and the time was reasonable considering the number of orders they were taking. I love Cuban food, and eat it often. I also cook it often (Made a killer Boliche last night, for instance). But I do like the food prepared in a traditional manner, unless the changes actually make it better. That didn't happen this time. Some of the recipes I use for my Cuban Sandwiches... notice no Mayo, no Salami: http://www.tasteofcuba.com/cubansandwich.html http://icuban.com/food/cuban_sandwich.html

Spring Roll was drenched in oil and over fried. And, this could not make for the good filling it had. The sauce served with the Spring Roll was the only edible thing. I really regretted tipping them before eating. I decided to give them another try and see how they serve on a weekday. I did tip again beforehand. I ordered the Mango Salad and Lo Men (with extra garlic and mushroom - for which I was charged .. going by last day's experience of flavorless Cho Men). The Mango Salad came out very well and the flavors really worked together. Lo Men was watery and salty in an almost humiliating way. And, I spotted two slices of mushroom and could not remotely taste any garlic. I was wondering why nobody comes and gets a feedback on the food here. Yea .. it depends on who is cooking today .. sorry about that. She simply walked away. And, that was it. Such a waste of money. Crap food after paying $17 for one. Memphis Blues BBQ House is not quite a fast food place, nor is it a typical restaurant. It comes with a higher price tag than a typical fast food place. I will say though that the gentleman bringing the food to the tables was very nice and gave the right amount of customer service I like. text: Taqueria El Bronco is the most popular restaurant on Cherokee Street, and that's saying a lot. Cherokee Street is known for its delicious Mexican food, and as time goes by, more and more restaurants are popping up to compete for the recent influx of hip, young customers. Taqueria El Bronco is still on top, though, and it's a position it mostly deserves. It's only my second-favorite taqueria on Cherokee Street, but it has a large menu and a selection of dirt cheap kool-aid-tasting margaritas that make it more of a crowd-pleaser than the smaller establishments. Taqueria El Bronco specializes in tortillas filled with grilled meat, and they're good at it. They're a lot less good at everything that isn't tortillas filled with meat: beans, rice, vegetables, salsa, etc. So if you visit Taqueria El Bronco --and you should; it's an institution-- you'll have the best experience if you order meat-and-tortilla dishes a la carte. Get the tacos; skip the rice.

text: After a jaunt to NOMA on a Friday night, we decided to get a late dinner at Santa Fe. Long timers here might remember the original location of Santa Fe on Frenchmen St. That restaurant opened in the 80's (I think) and was at the forefront of the Marigny revival. The menu was Mexican inspired, very creative, and well loved by food aficionados such as myself. The space too was beautiful and charming. In fact it was here that I was introduced to the straight up martini, much to my delight and ultimate chagrin. I always loved my evenings here. So it was with much sadness that the place did not re-open after the Storm. The restaurant was sold and re-opened on Esplanade in the space previously occupied by Greg Sonnier's Gabrielle, another favorite also shuttered by the Storm. I had been to the new Santa Fe only once and, for some reason, thought it to be simply a Tex Mex kind of place. I was totally wrong as I found out during my recent visit. Although the menu does contain Tex Mex staples such as nachos and quesadillas, the menu is well conceived and does homage to the original concept. We started off by splitting (thankfully because it was a huge portion) a special appetizer which was a salmon roulade. As I could tell, salmon was spread with goat cheese, seasoned , rolled, then battered and fried. It was served atop a curry/mustard cream sauce. It was outstanding in every way. My lovely dining companion ordered a chicken and portobello quesadilla, and I ordered seafood (shrimp and oyster) roll your own tacos served with guacamole, sour cream, lettuce tomato, and remoulade on the side. Both were very good choices. The space is nice too, very warm and inviting, lively without being out of control. The service was excellent and the prices were reasonable. Can't wait to go back.

text: Hobey's There are a LOT of people that steer away from one of my favorite haunts. Yes, it's in Sun Valley and that does not conjure up lots of warm fuzzies. This is a place where you would feel comfortable wearing a t-shirt and jeans. I started going to this place when I first moved to Reno back in 91. The restaurant looked a lot different then, but for a new college student with a limited income, this place, along with the Treasury Club (out of business) in Sparks, was perfect for weekend meals. Fast forward to today. Hobey's is still one of my favorite places! Every single day, they have a special. Sometimes, it's more special than others, but for the most part, as of this review, their specials run $6.95 and you get more than a fair shake for the buck! I do enjoy their salads. Yes, I said salads. Their Cob salad will not leave you hungry. The best part is the crumbled blue cheese on it! Even their Caesar salad is good. It comes with a sliced egg and asparagus. Not your normal Caesar, but it's good. When you come to this "casual" casino. Don't expect anything formal. Even their steak house is fairly casual. You will walk up to a small lectern and either be seated by the hostess or put your name in. If they took your name, it will be called and it can be heard nearly everywhere in the casino. Feel free to drop a nickle or two into their machines. Almost, as soon as you're seated, a busboy will come by and ask what you'd like to drink. Followed shortly by the waitress who will take your order. They are fast and so is the food preparation. With the exception of their salads, the food comes out HOT and fast. This place may not take the place on the most interesting food around, but they do have good food at a good price. Always have and I surmise, they always will. Perhaps one day I will try their steak house, but until then, this review is on their coffee shop. Service is good and if you're a regular, you get treated with an extra smile and some small talk. Which, for a neighborhood haunt, is nice. --------------------------------- Bottom Line Yes, I have come back and will continue to come back. Their food has always been decent to good. Service has always been good to very good.

text: Seriously, Tucson, start making the right restaurants popular (and start eating here more). They have a whole section of dosas I haven't tried yet. The ingredients are treated with respect. The preparation is light and healthy, the way Indian food should be. Not the heavy, greasy preparations found at the NY style Indian places in town. It's hard to believe people have gotten bad naan here, but every restaurant sends out bad food sometimes, so I'll believe those reviewers. However, both naans I've gotten here were perfect. Crispy bits on the outside, fully-cooked but steamy and pliant on the inside. The garlic naan had a hint of fennel that made it beautifully balanced. That sense of spice, coupled with the lightness of the preparations makes me suspect ayurvedic techniques at play, but that's a bit more than I understand about Indian cuisine. That quality and level of thought in the food makes the smaller portions/higher prices thing well worth it; you actually feel good after eating here. That said, the gulab jamon was second, or even third rate. Hard and dense in an uninteresting syrup, but truth be told, I've only once in my life had this dessert at a restaurant and thought it was better than second rate. So getting that dish right is a bonus, not a necessity, in my book. Missing one star because of the dessert, and I'd like to see a few other dishes on the menu, but maybe I'm being unfair on both counts. This might go to five after a couple more meals.

text: Hello cool weather, hello festival season! Heralding the gorgeous Fall season and Manayunk's Restaurant Week (9/14/15-9/25/15), the Manayunk StrEAT Festival takes over Main St and stretches from Shurs to Green. http://manayunk.com/signature-events/fall-streat-food-festival/ With a gorgeous day in the forecast, we took advantage of the seasonal closure of Martin Luther King Jr./West River Drive (April-Oct wknds) to bike to the festival. (Also wanted to burn calories and avoid driving ... because festival parking is as frustrating as the traffic). Vendors: * ~40 Food Trucks in attendance, as well as several arts/crafts, ice cream, wine/beer, and fashion trucks! Food prices vary, but most are in the festival-reasonable range of $4-$12. The wallet buster award goes to Surf and Turf for their $24 Surf and Turf Roll: Steak, lobster, kale, sundried tomato, and parmesan cheese. There was no line for this truck! * I noticed a high proportion of tots, mac+cheeses, and a multitude of pork products ... or maybe the fabulous smells and long lines of those units caught my eye more frequently. The trucks were well-clustered - there were a few strategic empty stretches on the street where folks have space to breathe. Omg I need a break!: * Most of the stores are open, allowing for a bit of quiet respite from the outdoor festivities. Spouse had a bike issue and stopped in Human Zoom for a quick repair. Whereas I underestimated the cooler temperatures and dropped by Philadelphia Runner for a pullover - giving it a road/bike trial run on the way home! I gotta go PP (cause, yea, you know me): * There are porta-loos strategically/discreetly placed around the festival. I did not use them, I did not smell them, I did not see serpentine lines leading to them. I even doubted they were there! Foot Traffic: * With the nice weather, the festival was quite busy but nowhere near the crushing insanity of Rittenhouse Row Festival. Pets are allowed, and strollers in abundance. Watch your step, and watch your pets! Notes: * Don't eat the morning of (and night before?) the festival to max stomach space for yums. * Walk on sidewalks for free smells (kitchen vents out the back of the trucks) * Walk on sidewalks to fast track to desired destination(s) * Bring cash - don't let a faulty card swipey thing stand in the way of noms! * Bike/take mass transit if possible - vehicle parking is scarce! Will definitely be back in Spring 2016 if weather permits!

text: Crab boxes made with LOVE! I was searching for Dungeness crab online and stumbled across this place. From the Old Hickory Blvd exit in Hermitage, it was about 15 minutes on the interstate right off of the 28th Ave exit on I-40 West, very convenient. It is located in a strip mall and not very visible from the road and when you walk in, it has a typical start-up restaurant feel to it with a small dining area that could fit about 20 people comfortably. The menu offerings and prices are good and what you would expect from a crab house. I placed my order for a Dungeness crab platter with a shrimp add on (the shrimp are pretty large for this area) and peach tea. As I sat at the table, I enjoyed the wall paintings of ocean scenery and watching ESPN and also noticed their health inspection score of 95--very respectable. When the box came out, I was impressed because you could tell it was made with love. From the bottom up, there was a layer of butter with minced garlic filling the entire bottom of the box about 1/4 inch deep and then sliced new potatoes, two really large broccoli florettes (stalks) and two ears of corn...and that was just leading up to the crab cluster. The Dungeness crab cluster was large and the shrimp were large too. Of course the whole box was covered with seafood seasoning and the box presented well and the food was great. Once I tried the peach tea (guessing it is homemade from the bottle it came in), it was so good, I bought 3 more bottles of it to go with me. This place needs more visibility and more customers!! If you like crab, you should give it a try.
label: POS

That aside, we're huge baseball fans and love to get out to the ballpark. But Tropicana Field lacks any real atmosphere compared to most Major League or even Grapefruit League parks. Your first look at the ball field will be disappointing. The artificial turf is worn and threadbare. Rather than an emerald green as in most ball parks, it looks unkempt. Yes, the domed stadium allows for a comfortable environment in the hot Florida climate and is a Godsend during those torrential rains that come rolling though periodically but at what price? This stadium needs to be torn down. On the plus side, the field is easy to get to by car with plenty of parking situated around the stadium. Local bars and eateries are located within easy walking distance. A major interstate road feeds the wide streets surrounding the stadium. Shuttles are available from local hotels. Inside the stadium there are fun things for kiddies including a ray (as in bat ray) petting and feeding pool. Good for one visit but it's baseball we're here for, isn't it? The Ted Williams Baseball Museum is worth the walk from wherever your seats are. It's a nice exhibit about the player who made his second home in the local area due of his love for fishing. Half of the exhibit (The Hitters Hall of Fame) pays homage to other baseball greats. Don't miss this. Of course, the reason for having this stadium is baseball. Tampa Bay has fielded excellent teams in major league's toughest division, but you'd never know it by the fan support. Visit the stadium and you're likely to see more fans wearing the opposing team's colors than the Rays'. That despite the Rays giving home team t's away quite often. It's not unusual to find the stadium less than 1/4 full even when the Rays are in first place. Most of the time the hometown fans seem uninvolved and need constant reminders to "cheer" or "make noise". With two strikes on an opposing batter, fans must be reminded (by a tootie horn) to unnerve the batter by ringing their cow bells. Really? Seriously? During the game there are other non-baseball distractions. Cheerleaders dancing on the dugout, a Sprite bottle racing a Pepsi bottle, a $5-a-chance lottery! OMG, crying in baseball would be an improvement over this! So the chance of building a new stadium is nil. Fan support is sorely lacking even though the Rays field a great team year after year. We would go more often if there weren't so many distractions. We love baseball and wish the Rays well but Tampa needs a better stadium and won't get one until they get better fans. Were I wrong, this place wouldn't have the worst attendance record in the league year after year. BTW, the two stars is out of respect for the Rays team. Go to see them and try to ignore the rest. If you've read the review this far you deserve a tidbit. If you should go, the Rays website charges $25 for advanced parking. Don't do it. Off site lots are $5 & $10. Rays' lots start at $15 during the week & $20 on weekends. If you go on a Sunday with 4+ people in your car, parking is FREE in ANY lot!

text: The infamous La Colombe, Frankford Ave...I want to give this barn like palace five stars but I just can't. Let's talk about the good stuff first... The artsy Fishtown location feels dominating and towering inside, like a large night club, but guess what? It works phenomenally for coffee and spirits! It's a breath of fresh air, compared to the average miniature coffee shop. After eating a chocolate chip muffin I decided to rob the place. I went to the counter and said, "Put all the pastries in my bag", "and put whatever doesn't fit, in your organic cardboard boxes". They stared. I frowned. Back to my seat. Yes, they are that good. I'm always impressed by the coffee selections, they live up to the unique descriptions. The fact that you can also get coffee been brewed beer adds a bit of fun and creativity to the menu. Feel free to skate around this palace and gauk at shiney espresso machines and beefy beer distillation machines... fancy-shmancy glam. You will find yourself surrounded by gigantic wooden doors, and bakers-a-bakin, I feel like I'm watching an Amish farm operate sometimes. It's very interesting. So far, so gooood... but then, disaster strikes.... LA COLOMBE HATES WHIPPED CREAM... They don't have this heavenly coffee balancing foam anywhere in the vaccinity. I thought to myself, are they a cult? What's going on!? I had to double check my surroundings, as I tripped over a little bit, I had to make sure I wasn't accidentally inducted in. I almost cried when I discovered this. I begged them for an alternative. Creme fresh? I don't know.. You can't mess with one of the best things to happen to my mouth since, ever. You might be the new coffee mob boss on the block, Godfather Colombe, but you can't mess with the Diety of the whipped! You're a whipped cream athiest. But I still accept you.. Ok, so I'll forgive you (cringing) for that. But should I get over the fact that your baristas seem like they are best friends Juno? I'm not the only one who feels like this btw. Every time I visit I feel like I'm being taken care of by a mr. or mrs. hipster neutrality. I noticed some batistas smile, but no one seems that cheerful. Maybe they need some whipped cream? But overall all the workers seem cool and smart! The waiters are the nicest of the bunch. The solution for more smiles= whipped cream. The seating looks great, and most of it is designed comfortably (even though you will only find solid wood for your tush..) but I miss a comfy couch or chair to study on. Comfort is half the reason I visit a coffee shop. It's still here. The rocking chair area is very comfy. Just no padding for the tush... The Amish nod. Did the owner grow up sleeping on a wooden bed? Honestly La Colombe is half in the 3 star zone, but makes up for it by going overboard into the 5 star zone, with great coffee and more. So that puts us at 4 stars. It's a mixed feeling kind of place, a fancy palace to take your out of town friends. It's already filled with touristy flockers. It's exciting but different. Thanks for the great coffee.

Disappointed we discussed her options for a new phone, but the only thing she cared about was that she was going to loose all of the pictures she had that had not been backed up in months. We decided to take the phone head home and see if there was some way that we could get the pictures from her phone. When we got home we quickly realized that without being able to enter in her pass code we were out of luck. However, this is where Reno iPhone repair comes into play. As a last ditch effort we decided that we would take it into these guys and see if maybe they could help us out. Well, help us out they did. We walked right up to their booth, did not wait a single minute to be seen (remember at apple it took us over an hour to be seen and we were there 15 minutes before apple opened), told them the situation, (Or I did, all she could tell them was that she wanted her pictures) and immediately they offered us some ideas. The gentleman behind the counter said what he could do was hook up a new screen, see if it powers on, and if it did they could get in and help her get her photos backed up via iCloud, then they could put her old screen back in, and they would only charge us $35 for their time. Great we said, lets do it. They immediately pulled her phone apart right in front of us, hooked up a new screen, and low and behold, it powered right up. The gentleman then checked a few things, powered down her phone and put her OLD screen back in. He told us her screen looked ok and that he wanted to check it one more time. He pressed the power button and it powered back up without any issue and we NO new parts. He checked the function of the screen said everything looked good, and put the whole phone back together. We left there less than 15 minutes after we came in, with no new parts, and a 100% functioning phone that APPLE told us could not be repaired. I can not give this company enough praise for their customer service, their skill and their honesty. If you have an iPhone hardware problem don't waste your time at the APPLE store, bring it here instead and be assured that everything that could be done has been done.

text: 8 weeks after opening this is possibly the newest addition to the St Pete trend of repurposed service-stations-turned-eateries. Urban Comfort offers interesting, high-quality cocktails and their own take on southern-urban comfort food. Three years ago I would have swooned myself unconscious over this place. However after being exposed to places like casita taqueria, queens head, and the repurposed warehouse/shop atmospheres of Green Bench and 3 Daughters breweries this place feels like the "next" in a group of new-concept yet retro, qualitycentric establishments. Don't misunderstand me....Urban Comfort is a very nice place, and I feel they do fulfill their tagline's proclamation of "Simple Foods Done Exceptionally Well." We had the Comfort Burger and Fresh Catch Fried Fish. In a word the burger was "substantial." It had a home made quality, and a beautiful bun that could not stand up to the deliciously meaty burger and indulgent toppings. A second bun on the side would have been a nice lifesaver while eating this monster. The half order of fried fish and hushpuppies we also ordered was good...not great. The biscuit was a bit dry and a little tough, but so were my grandma's, so....nostalgic. The creamed-corn was very good. I also enjoyed the cucumber salad....hand cut cukes in a lightly sweet solution...definitely made on site. Once again --remembrances of grandma's table. The last thing I'll mention is the attentive and professional server. She rightfully prepared me for the flavor of star anise in the Gin Gypsy cocktail, which was refreshing in the summer heat. While I wasn't crazy about the drink it was not the fault of the cocktail...just not my favorite flavor profile. I look forward to trying more food and drink at my next visit.

text: Absolutely horrid. Worst childcare mistake my husband and I have ever made in 3.5 years. Aside from a handful of staff who are genuinely excellent with children and seem to have real childcare experience, the rest are absolutely clueless about how to care for a child. The worst of all is Lee, the director, who I never once saw interact with any of the children, yet he felt it appropriate to lecture my husband and I daily about our parenting. Completely out of line and unprofessional. Though the facility claims to focus on the individual development and needs of each child there, in reality the children are grouped up and constantly shuffled around between different teachers and if a child doesn't fit into their "system", such as if a child doesn't nap for example, they are completely unprepared to accommodate that child's needs and instead choose to punish that child as if they were misbehaving. Takes a very conformist approach to childcare. A good child with a unique or spirited personality will have a very difficult time there if they don't conform to the formula. The "curriculum" is less focused on actual learning of useful skills and information and instead on teaching children about subjects they don't really need to be learning at their age. Is it nice that they told my daughter what "astronaut" is in Spanish? Sure. Did she really need to know it given that they don't actually teach Spanish in a way that children can truly learn it? No, I think not. If you're going to teach something, then teach it properly so that the student learns it not just memorized and regurgitates it on command like a parrot. That's not education, that's training. The facility itself is a series of closed isolating rooms and is always cold, no matter what the time of year or temperature. The daily activity reports are all pre-printed at the beginning of the day and generic. Nebulous scale for judging a child's behavior. Parents expected to correct bad behavior with almost no contextual information about it beyond generic footnotes such as "was disruptive in class" "not listening" and "yelling". Lee will swear up and down that he can accommodate any schedule since the facility is open 6am to 6:30pm, but in reality he DEMANDS that children (at least the preschoolers) be there no later than 9am every morning or they will be turned away. Likewise if a parent is even a little late picking up a child the facility will call child services and turn the child over to them. (Not hyperbole, actually stated in TLE rulebook.) They are heinously overpriced considering they can't even manage to wipe a child's nose or give the child a tissue to do it themselves. From feeding children the standard Sodexo fare of hamburgers and chicken nuggets for lunch everyday to the sad little cubby next the front desk with a filthy little mat on the floor they call an "infirmary", I could go on and on, however the very worst thing about this place was that my daughter who loves to learn and has been in daycare since she was 6 months old, HATED going there. She would literally cry and scream and beg us not to take her there EVERY. SINGLE. DAY. for 5 months until today when we finally had enough and said good bye to that place forever. I cannot stress enough that if you value your child's individual emotional and mental development then do not waste your time or money at The Learning Experience.

text: What gives? I have been to Dooners twice and twice I have been charged somewhere between $2.00 and $2.50 more than I should have been. The first time I did not notice until I looked at the receipt later, hours after I had left Dooners.This time I noticed when I sat down with my food. When I went back up to the counter, there were several people ordering and waiting for food so I decided to wait a few minutes. When the crowd cleared and I was able to make my way back to the counter, the young woman (the one who had made our sandwiches, not the one who had rung me up) had no idea what the charge was for and, because I was not given an itemized receipt, I could not make my inquiry more specific. In the meantime, the other woman --- the one who had rung me up --- was gone and I was told that no one knew when she would return. The young woman with whom I was having this conversation wasn't exactly rude but she did seem inconvenienced to have to answer my questions and address any issue other than scooping food into baskets. As for the food, it's fine. The concept provides for a quick and fairly hearty meal, though $7.19-$7.89 for a pita-style sandwich is pricey (not to mention the mysterious $2.00plus added on). I cannot help but make the comparison to Subway. It is the same order from-a-bar-of-ingredients-and-choose-a-bread-on-which-to-put-the-ingredients idea. There are two kinds of cabbage, two kinds of legumes, olives, a tomato-onion mixture, etc. I cannot say that the above mentioned ingredients were particularly un-fresh or poorly presented nor can I say that there was anything remarkable about any of them or the way they were prepared. Unfortunately, my husband thought his lamb-beef was a bit stale. Still, for the food and the convenience of it on a busy Saturday night in a downtown area, I would give a solid three stars. For the random upcharge and no-one's ability to explain it to me, I have to take Dooners to task. Furthermore, it appears that others have had the same problems.

text: Once upon a time, this old curmudgeon attended Uni in England. One day a visiting Indian professor/Chef moved in to an open room in the flat for 6 months. Since I was the only American who was brave enough to try her food, she tended to cook a lot for her and I and her husband (he was in another flat for some reason). I learned a lot during that time. I learned about looking past cultures and connecting with the people. I also learned about how spices worked together to make a new thing that is greater than the parts. It was the best Indian food I had ever tasted (She was a Doctor of Indian Culture and Cuisine whose family had many old and successful restaurants back in India) and had never tasted after...20+ years later. I have had a few places that were pretty good. Here in New Orleans, it's a bit harder but Nola Desi was fantastic and probably the best in the area...until now. But just like taking a bite out of some fried chicken that was exactly as good as grams used to make. Or like that piece of apple pie that you know was just like that one weird aunt that baked too many pies because she was bored. Eating here was like going back in time. This was the most PERFECTLY authentic Indian food I've had since that wonderful woman in Uni! Spiced perfectly (He brought my dish out and then took it back before I could try it because he KNEW by looking at me that I really did want it spicy and it wasn't spicy enough), cooked amazingly well. As someone else mentioned, the portions look small but they will fill you up (Even Fat Man was happy). The Girly had the Saag Shrimp. I don't like saag much usually but I really loved the saag here., Fat Man had the Goat with lentils. The goat was delicious and pot-roast tender, strongly flavored, spicy and with a wonderful aroma and sweat inducing heat. The lentils were perfectly cooked. We both had unsweetened iced tea (really light with very low tannin...maybe white tea?) We also shared an order of falafel (SUPER crispy on the outside, creamy on the inside) which came out with a small salad, 2 dressings and sitting on top of the most brilliant paratha which was soaked in ghee. It was flaky, chewy and buttery. The staff were fantastic and wonderfully polite (Even to the large and annoying family in the corner with not 1, not 2 but 3 screaming babies). The place is little so it was like knives going through our temples. Even though we didn't order dessert, He brought us out a rather plentiful portion of something called Lentil Halwa. It was hot and I didn't think I would like it but it was delicious. A must have in the winter. I don't give any place 5 stars until I've eaten there 3 times but I'm looking forward to that 5th star. I am 100% a fan of this place and the wonderful people who run it. P.S. Don't be one of THOSE people who order things extra-spicy and then get upset because it's spicy. You make it hard on the rest of us who LIKE spicy and you cost the restaurant money because they have to lose the money from the plate YOU ordered due to having to replace it with wussy stuff.

text: As someone who has been in arenas in most major cities across the US and Canada, I think the current version of the Ice Palace/TBT Forum/Amalie Arena is right there with the best of them. The last few years, I've attended Lightning games, Storm games and concerts here and continue to see improvements or enhancements virtually every visit. I hear that even more are coming, namely to add table-top loge seating similar to Amway Center in Orlando and major upgrades to make the second level a true club level experience. Also, once the current agreement with Bright House expires, the plan is to exponentially increase the amount of hotspots in the building so we can actually talk, text and post to social media from these events. While my personal opinion is that the in-game presentation is too loud and the in-arena Lightning Vision host should be working at Buddy's instead of doing segments sponsored by Buddy's, the arena offers a very comfortable experience with good sightlines for sports and acoustics for concerts I've attended recently like Katy Perry, Selena Gomez and Van Halen. Cleanliness and customer service are clearly a priority to Jeff Vinik, as I have rarely encountered anything to suggest otherwise when entering the building, on the concourses, the restrooms or inside the seating bowl. There's a reason why the Lightning are playing to over 97% capacity the last two seasons while the Buccaneers, Rays and USF have thousands of unsold tickets. The one suggestion I would make is to evaluate how to better the Will Call experience for those of us who pick up tickets right before an event. It is nice that the area is indoors, but it is often quite chaotic and there aren't enough windows in my opinion to keep things moving. Too often, a customer at the only window for say last names ending T-Z has an issue and it isn't a quick pick-up and go. This slows the line for the rest of us who have no issues...so multiple windows for each alphabetical category would alleviate some of these delays. Sure, I wish food, beer and alcohol pricing at concessions were a bit lower, but most of us feel that way these days when attending events virtually anywhere. At least the Lightning do offer season-ticket holders a 25% discount, so nicely ask the person next to you wearing the STM patch on their blue jersey to buy you the item, give them money and they'll probably do it. Now, if Ben Bishop can be a legitimate playoff-caliber goaltender, we may really enjoy being in this building in the coming months.

Takumi is a perfect example. They market themselves as "authentic Japanese, but serve a fusion of Asian food styles. Today, we both ordered the #1 Bento Box which comes with teriyaki chicken, shrimp/vegi tempura, salad, white rice, and chef's choice sashimi... I never got to the sashimi. I was put off before even getting to it. The teriyaki chicken tasted strange...almost like turkey..and the sauce was bland. It carried no taste at all and certainly would not be identified as anything resembling teriyaki in a blind taste test. Teriyaki should either be slightly sweet or even spicy, either way it should be flavorful enough to taste. Turning to the tempura for solace I was again disappointed when met with a droopy, soggily coated shrimp without an ounce of taste! It seemed quite amazing to me that a chef could remove "taste" from not one, but 2 food sources. The salad ...everyday iceberg lettuce...I would later find out, swims in bottled Benihana salad dressing. The dressing had taste at least! Feeling like I simply did not want to partake in a meal that I wasn't enjoying and it is my birthday, I explained to the waitress that I was dissatisfied with the quality of the meal, I ask if she would please trade it in for a simple California Roll. Well, apparently removing taste is a habit of Takumi's owner as I was tastelessly told "no" that I could not do that. I was offered to replace the teriyaki chicken with some Chinese dish which I did not ask for, nor want. At this point I am wondering who runs this place...he/she who cares so little about customer service. I ask the waitress to please send the manager out. I gentleman approached the table to inform us that the manager was not there and that I could "talk to me". I ask "and who is me? What is your position here?" Astoundingly, this man replied "the owner". Really? And this is how you present yourself? I should not be surprised since he clearly has little concern for his foods presentation either. I explain my side and ask why I cannot get the California Roll iu ask for in lieu of the meal I dislke. I'm told by the supposed owner of Takumi that no one else today has complained. Please note that there is one..yes one...other party of 3 in the restaurant. So, basically I've been told that my opinion is invalid..but, of course my money is not. There followed more banter without once even a glimpse of an explanation as to why giving me what I want was not an option. Did I need to pay a difference? Did I need to know an ancient Japanese code? Nope, just pissed the owner off that I questioned the quality of the food. When i ask if the tempura was frozen he would not confirm or deny. My other half ask if he tasted the food from his kitchen. "sometimes" was the owners answer. Sometimes??? Really??? If you don't know what your food taste like then don't serve it and certainly don't reprimand someone who tells you that the taste is a problem. I have no idea what kind of business Takumi does, but I believe that anyone who is familiar with authentic Asian cuisine will not find Takumi satisfying.

text: We did a sea kayak tour on Santa Cruz island. We got the boat from Ventura. It's quite easy to find and plenty of parking. Arrive a little early so that you can complete forms. There are other kayak tours and campers and day hikers leaving from this spot so you have to find the right check in person. But that is no problem at all. The boat ride over is about an hour. If u get sea sick take some Dramamine before hand. There are snacks and drinks to buy on the boat. Once you arrive you head to the kayaks where they will go through a safety and education piece. Don't worry if you've never kayaked before there are all levels here. You can store your stuff in a big container while you kayak. Bring some water and maybe a snack for the kayak tour. Depending on the temp u may feel cold and they have jackets and bottoms u can borrow and wear as u will get very wet and inside the caves can be chilly. We did not feel we needed them and it was overcast when we were there. You'll kayak for a couple of hours. It's tiring! Be aware of this :) but so much fun. The caves are incredible and the guides are knowledgeable fun and safe. They will help you if you need it. One of our party got exhausted and one of the guides just towed them. When you get back you can then hike or snorkel. They provide wet suits and all the gear. There is nothing on the island, so bring food and water with you and a change of clothing, again if the temps are low u will want to have something warm to put on. I really enjoyed this trip it was probably one of the best kayak tours I've done.

text: I recently took my 1974 Mercedes Roadster to Rex Carle Automotive for some engine, brake system and electrical work. In searching for the "right guy" to do the work on my car, I asked around and all signs pointed to Rex -- including that he is a Bosch Authorized Repair Center which is a critically important detail, especially when servicing Mercedes engine & fuel systems. Immediately upon meeting Rex during an initial inspection of the car, it was blatantly evident that he is the real deal. Very knowledgeable, detail oriented, and genuine. I felt instantly comfortable with his ability to do the right job and take care of my classic Mercedes. After working up a list of parts include an entire rebuild of the fuel injection hose system (no small feat when done properly); check valves, replacing all brake lines, rebuilding brake reservoir, belts, oil, ps cleanup, fix a misfire, adjust surging idle, inspection and fix turn signal, we set a date to drop the car. Dropped the car on a Monday morning and told him to take whatever time was needed. Picked the car up on Thursday morning. WOW would be an understatement. The moment I started the car, you could tell it was running "as delivered" from the dealership. This car had been in our family since 1979 and I hadn't heard it sound like this since the 80's. Idle, perfect. Not a drop of movement or shake on the tachometer. Smooth and silky. Took the car out and up the hill -- the tires actually spun! (not that i'm doing that in my 74 -- but it happened). On the highway home, I was smiling at how well the car worked again. Plus, Rex fixed my turn signal switch. These parts are NLA and he just took it apart and fixed it. I can't express enough how professional, honest, genuine and great an experience it is to work with Rex and his team. Cost? How much is it worth to have the right job done to your favorite car... But seriously, very competitive and I haven't thought about the cost after feeling the result. Take your favorite Mercedes to Rex is my advice.

We all raved about the first 3-salad course of eggplant, carrot, and cucumbers. Don't hold back on the pita. Grab 3 or 4 because you'll need them to help grab the veggies! The second course of B'stella was great! By looking at the towels around me, this was the messiest dish. The third course of spicy chicken literally fell off the bone, and was very flavorful. It came out super hot, so the pitas that came around helped. For our fourth course, we chose the lamb with almonds and honey over the beef. The lamb did not disappoint, and the honey definitely added just the right amount of sweetness. By this time, all of us were stuffed, yet we had two more courses! The couscous was probably our least favorite since it had to follow some strong dishes. Thankfully, the fruit and delicious mint tea helped slow things down. Baklava was also a nice treat, thought it wasn't anything to write home about. Overall, I'd recommend this place. For date nights, group dinners, and large celebrations. Since it was such a large feast, perhaps slowing down the pace will help! Service was friendly, and since we were there during the weekend, we did get to see a few belly dancers pass through. The stuffed pizzas only come in large but should probably considered a double-large. As the name would suggest, the toppings are stuffed between two crusts. The top crust seemed to be dusted with garlic, oil and parmesan cheese adding an extra magic to the pie. There was a great Italian flavor with each bite. Even the broccoli rabe tasted fresh and nicely seasoned. Despite two layers of crust and a large amount of fillings, it was still manageable to pick up or cut with a knife and fork. Unfortunately, I didn't love the eggplant parm sandwich which I also ordered and will be deducting a star from my review. It wasn't well breaded and the eggplant was just of ok quality. The sauce, cheese bread and eggplant didn't blend together as an eggplant parmesan sandwich should. Eggplant parm sandwiches are a dime a dozen in Philly, but the stuffed pizza was so amazing and unique that I won't let the sandwich get me down. Between the sandwiches and pizza, we had leftovers. The pizza tasted awesome hot & fresh, but then amazing cold out of the fridge. We ordered through Grubhub and the delivery came within about an hour on a Friday night. Not a fan of the hush puppies because it's fried but for people who loved fried foods this may be for you. We had the corn and squash soup (I believe) & a salad. The soup was phenomenal! It reminder me of a cold corn chowder..the salad was very fresh but too salty for my taste. I think my friend and I are sensitive to salty foods so we'd prefer not to get that again. For our third course we got the pork loin chop which was cooked perfectly - juicy and easy to cut ..yum! The sauce which was like a barbecue was tastey. We also got the sea bass which had a delicious crispy skin on top of a seasoned grilled corn..yum! Lastly to finish off the night, we had the banana toffee pudding and a peach breadding...correct me if I recalled it wrongly. All in all a great experience. I'd definitely come here again for a date in the future or restaurant week simply because I can't afford meals like this on a regular basis, but I'm so glad I made the trip!

Now for the ugly: the price tags were just too much. We were hopeful that we could find a new shower head and mixer for around $500. Most of them started closer to $800, though. We did end up buying Delta products through the Ferguson website, where we found more reasonable prices.
